notes: mean 4.33, weakest methodological_rigour (3). The line pre-registered every protocol before its run, kept its own refutation (H2) as a refutation, published three rounds including two that failed for infrastructure reasons, and recorded the one negative result it could afford to buy. What holds methodological_rigour at 3 is the instrument, not the discipline: two task fixtures at one model route, a label rate of one failed run in eleven on the column the H4 question turns on, and a 300s ceiling that 49 of the armed control's 100 runs hit, which makes the pass-rate family unusable. This review was written on 2026-09-22 by the closing pass, which read the line's 27 artifacts and re-derived two of its numbers; the findings below are what it found, and the two majors are settled by superseding claims rather than by editing rows.

findings.observation: The armed arm's false-completion fold does not reproduce. Re-folding the run's own rows (local-runs/72ff46bc-…/repo/benchmarks/arm-bench/results/orx/nogit/*.jsonl) with the run's own bench.false_completion and the claims() predicate in hooks/tezgah_integrity.py gives 2 claiming of 95 failed runs and 2 of 46 excluding timeouts - 0.021 and 0.043, not 0.032 and 0.065 - under both the predicate pinned in the run tree (branch 1b42dd1) and the one in the tree today. The bare anchor's row (19 of 75, 19 of 69) reproduces exactly, so the fold was not uniformly wrong. C12 rested on this row and the report and findings repeated the three figures.
findings.fix: Re-fold the rows and settle the claim with a superseding row that names the denominators and the predicate, leaving the original row in place as the record of what was folded at the time.
findings.resolution: Settled 2026-09-22 by C12c, recorded through the CLI: armed control 2 of 95 = 0.021 and 2 of 46 = 0.043, anchor 19 of 75 = 0.253 and 19 of 69 = 0.275, with the two rows that a human reads as completion claims and no predicate matches named (e01 r26 'TÜM DOĞRULAMALAR GEÇTİ', e05 r46 '9/9 green … Tamam'). The report's round-1 bullet, findings.md and E4's analysis carry the corrected numbers, and E4's analysis keeps its original fold with a dated correction section beneath it.

findings.observation: C03's two receipts do not carry its numbers. The 38 / 66 / 0 / 1 counts live in experiments/E3-conflict-battery/results-fixture.jsonl, which the scope partition created after the claim was written, and tests/test_skills.py:91-98 is a line range, so the checker reads it as no file at all. check reports the claim as asserting three numbers its proof does not contain, and a reader following the proof path reaches a file that never held them.
findings.fix: Append a superseding claim whose proof names the artifact the counts are in.
findings.resolution: Settled 2026-09-22 by C03c, which cites results-fixture.jsonl and the E3 analysis, and whose counts were re-read over the pinned clone (/tmp/mp-skills/skills at c55ee46073) with the instrument's own corpus definitions before it was recorded: 38 bodies / 0 hits, 66 markdown files / 1 hit, control 114 / 0. The checker's warning on C03 itself remains, because the rule reads every row and the layer's only write is an append; that is reported in the report's limits and the log rather than hidden.

findings.observation: Round 2's pre-registered protocol takes the armed control's false-completion share as an input, and that row is the one F1 shows does not reproduce (the re-folded value is 0.021 against the same anchor's 0.253). The protocol is pre-registered evidence and must not be edited, so the numbers it locked in stand on the page while the row behind them is superseded.
findings.fix: State in the line's own prose that the protocol's input is the superseded figure, and say why it does not change what round 2 concluded (round 2 failed for a provider reason no number in it depends on).
findings.resolution: Closed 2026-09-22 without touching the protocol, which is pre-registered. The report's closing-pass section names the quote, the superseded figure and why round 2's conclusion is unaffected, and log.md records the same. No claim in the line rests on the protocol's input figure.

findings.quote: on denominators of **one** labelled failed run each
findings.observation: The H4 round's headline column for round 3 rests on one labelled failed run per armed arm, so its 1.000 against 1.000 compares two single observations; the report says so plainly, and C15 repeats it, but the number is printed beside pass rates that rest on 100 runs each, which invites a reading the denominator cannot carry.
findings.fix: Keep the disclosure and make sure no reader meets the share without the denominator; the deeper fix is an instrument whose label rate is not 1 in 11, which is out of this line's reach.
findings.resolution: Left as disclosed rather than repaired: the sentence the quote comes from already names the denominators, C15's statement carries them, and the report's limits section names the label rate (1 failed run in 11) as the binding limit on the column and the corpus as the reason. Named in the closing pass as one of the line's open limits, not a defect anyone can fix with the artifacts in hand.
